beats.beat: The product set sits in two halves. The chemicals half is functional additives and chemically modified minerals; the minerals half is soft minerals and hard minerals. The company processes mineral feedstock and sells the output to industrial users.

Sales are not contracted in advance. The company relies on purchase orders rather than long-term or definitive agreements to set volume, pricing and other terms — and names that reliance itself as a risk factor.
That leaves it dependent on a small set of buyers: the top 10 customers accounted for about 59%, 57% and 59% of revenue from operations in FY2015, FY2016 and FY2017.

Distribution runs through the family. A long-term arrangement with corporate promoter 20 Microns Limited lets the company sell through the promoter's network, and the DRHP lists 'support of our holding company' among its strengths.
Exports are small and narrow. Over the past five years the company shipped ₹1,068.18 lakh, about ₹10.68 crore, to three markets: Nigeria, Saudi Arabia and Sri Lanka.

The DRHP's own strengths list runs to a diversified product portfolio, diversified user industries, import substitution, product innovation and continuous R&D, and the management team. What the excerpt set does not contain: revenue split by product family or vertical, any named customer, plant capacities, or headcount.

beats.beat: The restated statement of profit and loss covers six periods: FY2013 to FY2017, plus the six months ended September 30, 2017. Profit after tax: (₹0.27 crore) in FY2013, (₹0.12 crore) in FY2014, ₹1.50 crore in FY2015, ₹0.90 crore in FY2016, ₹1.75 crore in FY2017 and ₹1.33 crore in the six months to September 30, 2017. The company moved from losses to profits in FY2015 and has stayed profitable since.

Basic earnings per share, on shares of ₹10 face value, moves the same way: (₹0.45), (₹0.20), ₹2.47, ₹1.46, ₹2.43 and ₹1.48 across FY2013, FY2014, FY2015, FY2016, FY2017 and the six months to September 30, 2017.

Cash generated by operations was positive in the first four periods: ₹2.01 crore, ₹1.28 crore, ₹4.22 crore and ₹8.03 crore across FY2013 to FY2016. Then it turned: an outflow of ₹3.50 crore in FY2017, followed by an inflow of ₹1.25 crore in the six months to September 30, 2017.

The filing treats that reversal as a risk in its own right, stating that the company had negative cash flows in previous financial years and that sustained negative cash flow could affect growth. That makes the FY2017 operating outflow the single most informative number in the restated cash flow statement.
Total assets moved from ₹30.19 crore at March 2013 down to ₹25.93 crore at March 2015, then rebuilt to ₹32.74 crore at March 2017 and ₹34.25 crore at September 30, 2017.
The capital base as at September 30, 2017 was ₹8.97 crore of issued, subscribed and paid-up equity — 89,70,000 shares of ₹10 each — against authorised capital of ₹20.00 crore.

What the excerpted statements do not carry: revenue from operations, EBITDA, and borrowings or total debt. No revenue line appears in the digest for any of the six periods, so no revenue trend and no margin can be computed from this material.

beats.beat: Four promoters are named: Mr. Chandresh S. Parikh, Mr. Atil C. Parikh, Mr. Rajesh C. Parikh and the corporate promoter 20 Microns Limited.

Between them the promoters hold 89,48,270 equity shares, or 99.76% of the pre-issue paid-up capital. The promoter group excluding the promoters holds another 21,510 shares, or 0.24%. Practically the whole company is on the inside before the offer.

Related-party transactions have run through the accounts in each of the last five financial years and in the six months ended September 30, 2017, and the filing flags the risk that future related-party dealings could affect financial condition and results of operations.

The compliance record carries marks. There have been non-filings, incorrect filings and delays in filing statutory forms with the Registrar of Companies, later filed with additional fees; certain statutory and regulatory licences, registrations and approvals have not yet been obtained for the Plot 9-10, GIDC Waghodia facility; and the corporate logo is not yet registered.

Asset ownership is partial. The company does not own the premises at its manufacturing facilities at Plot 347, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, Gujarat and Plot 104/3, Thenkasi Road, Pathur Village, Alangulam, Tirunelveli, Tamil Nadu, nor at its administrative offices in Bhuj and Udaipur.

Balance-sheet obligations to weigh alongside the equity story: contingent liabilities and commitments not provided for aggregated ₹29.11 lakh as at September 30, 2017; unsecured loans taken by the company, promoters, group companies or associates can be recalled by lenders at any time; and loan agreements carry restrictive covenants and certain unconditional rights in favour of lenders.
The company, its promoters, group company and directors are parties to legal proceedings, which the filing lists as the first internal risk factor.
Not in the excerpts: any auditor qualification or adverse remark, any regulator's penalty order, and the amounts, counterparties or current status of the legal proceedings.

beats.beat: Specialty chemicals is the slice of the chemicals industry that sells on performance rather than volume: small tonnages, specific functions. CRISIL sizes the Indian chemicals industry excluding pharmaceuticals and fertilisers at ₹5,800–6,200 billion in fiscal 2017, with specialty chemicals excluding agrochemicals and dyestuffs at roughly 17% of that, about ₹1,000 billion.

The segment grew at 10–12% CAGR from fiscal 2014 to 2017, and CRISIL forecasts 12–14% CAGR ahead; it is projected to reach ₹1,443 billion. Within it, sub-segments run at 10% to 15% CAGR, with construction chemicals, water chemicals and personal care ingredients at the top of that range.

This is a fragmented market, not a consolidated one. SMEs hold 70–75% of it, and the filing notes only a few Indian players have the scale or capability to compete with global giants on product development and innovation.

The demand drivers the filing names: rising intensity of consumption, end-use demand from a middle class it projects at 148 million households by 2030, improved consumption standards, the Draft National Chemical Policy, and 100% foreign direct investment being permitted in the sector.

Two downstream industries the filing also sizes: the domestic paints market at ₹401 billion in fiscal 2017, and the organised cosmetics and toiletries market at ₹430–460 billion. The filing does not say how much of this company's revenue comes from either.

The headwinds it concedes: India's chemicals industry imported more than it exported in every year from 2012-13 to 2016-17, with imports growing at 6.4% CAGR against exports at 6%; chemical exports to Europe face the REACH registration regime; and GST replaced the earlier indirect tax stack from July 1, 2017.

beats.beat: 20 Microns Nano Minerals processes and sells specialty chemicals — functional additives and chemically modified minerals, plus soft minerals and hard minerals — from plants in Gujarat and Tamil Nadu.
It does not go to market on its own. A long-term arrangement with its corporate promoter, 20 Microns Limited, lets it market and sell through the promoter's network.
The company has filed a DRHP to list on the SME platform of the NSE (NSE EMERGE), with Vivro Financial Services Private Limited as lead manager and Link Intime India Private Limited as registrar.

The excerpt set states the objects of the offer but not its size: the money is earmarked for capex at a new facility at Plot 336, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, Gujarat and for general corporate purposes. No issue size, price band, or split between fresh shares and a sale by existing holders appears in these excerpts.
Scale, in one line: profit after tax of ₹1.75 crore in FY2017 on total assets of ₹32.74 crore, against ₹0.90 crore of profit in FY2016.

beats.beat: This is a filing, not a priced offer. The excerpt set does not disclose the issue size, the price band, the number of shares on offer, the split between a fresh issue and an offer for sale, or the name of any selling shareholder. Anything said about those would be invention.

The objects that are stated are specific. The first is capital expenditure to set up a new manufacturing facility at Plot 336, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, Gujarat. The second is general corporate purposes.

There is a third, non-financial object: creating a public trading market for the equity shares by listing them on the SME platform of the NSE (NSE EMERGE), which the filing frames as a way to raise visibility and brand.
The named intermediaries are Vivro Financial Services Private Limited as lead manager and Link Intime India Private Limited as registrar.

Context for the capex object: the company does not own the premises at its existing manufacturing facilities at Plot 347, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, Gujarat and Plot 104/3, Thenkasi Road, Pathur Village, Alangulam, Tirunelveli, Tamil Nadu. The offer's first object adds a third site.

offer.heading: The offer and what the money is for
offer.purpose: State the offer's disclosed objects and named intermediaries, and be explicit about the structural facts the excerpts do not give.

beats.beat: One operating plant does not yet have the approvals it needs. Certain statutory and regulatory licences, registrations and approvals required to operate the manufacturing facility at Plot 9-10, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, Gujarat have not been obtained, and the filing says it cannot assure the company will not be penalised for the non-compliance — with the consequence stated as an adverse effect on operations and financial condition.

Revenue is concentrated and not locked in. There are no long-term or definitive customer agreements; volume, pricing and other terms are governed by purchase orders, and the top 10 customers produced about 59% of revenue from operations in FY2017, 57% in FY2016 and 59% in FY2015.

It depends on its promoter to sell. Products go to market through the network of corporate promoter 20 Microns Limited under a long-term arrangement, which the DRHP lists among the company's strengths; the same relationship puts related-party transactions at the centre of the accounts, and the filing accepts it may keep entering into them.

Operations consumed cash in FY2017. After ₹8.03 crore of operating inflow in FY2016, the company recorded a ₹3.50 crore outflow in FY2017, and the filing states plainly that it had negative cash flows in previous financial years and that sustained negative cash flow could affect growth and business.

The company and the people behind it are in legal proceedings. The company, its promoters, group company and directors are parties to certain legal proceedings, and the filing warns that an adverse decision may have a material adverse effect on business, results of operations and financial condition.

beats.beat: Valuing an issue normally means putting the company's earnings beside the earnings multiples of listed peers. The excerpt set contains no peer comparison table, no named listed peers, and no peer P/E, EPS, NAV or RoNW — so a peer table cannot be built from the material supplied.

There is also no price band, no issue size and no post-issue share count in the excerpts. A price-to-earnings ratio needs a price on top and earnings per share underneath; the earnings are here, the price is not. Without peer multiples as well, no implied price range can be derived from this filing as supplied.

What is disclosed is one whole side of that calculation: basic EPS of (₹0.45), (₹0.20), ₹2.47, ₹1.46, ₹2.43 and ₹1.48 for FY2013, FY2014, FY2015, FY2016, FY2017 and the six months to September 30, 2017, on a base of 89,70,000 shares of ₹10 each.
NAV per share and return on net worth are not in the excerpt set either, so the other two figures a peer table normally carries cannot be filled in from this material.
